All 24 tests pass. The implementation in `list_ops.py` is complete:

- **`append(list1, list2)`** — recursively prepends the head of `list1` and appends the rest to `list2`
- **`concat(lists)`** — flattens one level by recursively `append`-ing each sublist
- **`filter(function, list)`** — keeps elements for which the predicate is true, recursively
- **`length(list)`** — counts by recursing on the tail
- **`map(function, list)`** — applies the function to the head and recurses on the tail
- **`foldl(function, list, initial)`** — recurses left-to-right, updating the accumulator with `function(acc, el)`
- **`foldr(function, list, initial)`** — recurses right-to-left; the accumulator is updated with the rightmost element first (`foldr(f, list[:-1], f(acc, list[-1]))`), which is the subtle ordering the spec warns about and what the direction-dependent division test (`24` → `9`) checks
- **`reverse(list)`** — recursively rebuilds the list in reverse order

Per the spec, no existing helper functions (`len`, `reversed`, `itertools`, etc.) are used — only recursion, indexing, and `+`. No files were created or modified other than `list_ops.py`, and `list_ops_test.py` is untouched.
